claims.text: Dose: 200 mg (any formulation) as soon as possible within 72 hours after oral, vaginal, or anal sex; maximum 200 mg per 24 hours
claims.quote: the recommended dose of 200 mg of doxycycline (any formulation) to be taken as soon as possible within 72 hours after having oral, vaginal, or anal sex with a maximum dose of 200 mg every 24 hours.

claims.text: Across three large randomized trials, more than 70% reduction in syphilis and chlamydia and about 50% in gonorrhea (key takeaway, evidence section, FAQ, citable summary, SVG chart)
claims.quote: In three large randomized controlled trials, 200 mg of doxycycline taken within 72 hours after sex has been shown to reduce syphilis and chlamydia infections by >70% and gonococcal infections by approximately 50%.

claims.text: CDC recommends providers counsel MSM and transgender women with a bacterial STI (syphilis, chlamydia, or gonorrhea) in the past 12 months
claims.quote: Providers should counsel all gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (MSM) and transgender women (TGW) with a history of at least one bacterial sexually transmitted infection (STI)

claims.text: ...specifically syphilis, chlamydia, or gonorrhea, in the past 12 months
claims.quote: (specifically, syphilis, chlamydia or gonorrhea) during the past 12 months about the benefits and harms of using doxycycline

claims.text: ...and offer doxy PEP through shared decision-making
claims.quote: of oral, vaginal, or anal sex and should offer doxycycline postexposure prophylaxis (doxy PEP) through shared decision-making.

claims.text: Strong recommendation backed by high-quality evidence
claims.quote: High-quality evidence supports this strong recommendation to counsel MSM and TGW and offer doxy PEP.

claims.text: The trials that showed benefit enrolled MSM and transgender women
claims.quote: three large randomized controlled trials among MSM and transgender women (TGW) studied STI PEP in the form of 200 mg of doxycycline taken after sex. These trials all demonstrated significant reductions in bacterial STI acquisition

claims.text: Providers may discuss doxy PEP with MSM and TGW without a recent bacterial STI who plan sex that raises exposure risk; not directly studied
claims.quote: Although not directly assessed in the trials included in these guidelines, doxy PEP could be discussed with MSM and TGW who have not had a bacterial STI diagnosed during the previous year but will be participating in sexual activities

claims.text: No CDC recommendation for cisgender women, cisgender heterosexual men, transgender men, or other queer and nonbinary people (replaces "not recommended for")
claims.quote: No recommendation can be given at this time on the use of doxy PEP for cisgender women, cisgender heterosexual men, transgender men, and other queer and nonbinary persons.

claims.text: Evidence insufficient to assess balance of benefits and harms in these groups
claims.quote: Evidence is insufficient to assess the balance of benefits and harms of the use of doxy PEP

claims.text: CDC asks providers to use clinical judgment and shared decision-making for people outside its recommendation
claims.quote: providers should use their clinical judgement and shared decision-making to inform use of doxy PEP with populations that are not part of CDC recommendations.

claims.text: Kenyan women trial: gonorrhea not significantly reduced (CDC summary)
claims.quote: It found no significant reduction in bacterial STIs (RR: 0.88; 95% CI = 0.60–1.29), chlamydia (RR: 0.73; 95% CI = 0.47–1.13), or gonorrhea (RR: 1.64; 95% CI = 0.78–3.47)

claims.text: Syphilis could not be evaluated because only two early syphilis infections occurred
claims.quote: Syphilis efficacy could not be evaluated because there were only two early syphilis infections during the study.

claims.text: DOXYVAC initial results: syphilis 79% lower, chlamydia 89% lower, gonorrhea 51% lower (table, labeled initial results)
claims.quote: Initial results demonstrated that doxy PEP was associated with significant reductions in gonorrhea (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]: 0.49; 95% CI = 0.32–0.76), chlamydia (aHR: 0.11; 95% CI = 0.04–0.30), and syphilis (aHR: 0.21; 95% CI = 0.09–0.47)

claims.text: 12-month DoxyPEP follow-up: tetracycline-resistant S. aureus in the nose rose from 5% to 13% in the doxy PEP arm; no change in the standard-of-care arm (body, key takeaway, figure, FAQ)
claims.quote: had an increase in tetracycline-resistant(from 5% [20 of 428] to 13% [28 of 222]). There was no change in carriage or resistance in the standard of care arm

claims.text: Doxy PEP targets bacterial STIs (syphilis, chlamydia, gonorrhea) and does not prevent HIV; people at risk of HIV need HIV PrEP alongside it
claims.quote: Doxy PEP, when offered, should be implemented in the context of a comprehensive sexual health approach, including risk reduction counseling, STI screening and treatment, recommended vaccination and linkage to HIV PrEP, HIV care, or other services as appropriate.

claims.text: People living with HIV should be linked to HIV care
claims.quote: Confirm or encourage linkage to HIV care for persons living with HIV infection.

claims.text: Doxy PEP offered as part of comprehensive sexual health care, alongside condoms, HIV PrEP, vaccination and testing
claims.quote: Doxy PEP, when offered, should be implemented in the context of a comprehensive sexual health approach, including risk reduction counseling, STI screening and treatment, recommended vaccination and linkage to HIV PrEP

claims.text: CDC lists hepatitis A, hepatitis B, HPV and mpox vaccines among services to consider
claims.quote: Screen for hepatitis B and C infection; vaccinate against hepatitis B if susceptible. Administer other vaccines as indicated (mpox, hepatitis A, and human papillomavirus).

claims.text: Side effects CDC highlights: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, esophageal irritation, sun sensitivity; most common in FAQ
claims.quote: known side effects such as photosensitivity, esophagitis and esophageal discomfort, gastrointestinal intolerance (nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea)

claims.text: Doxycycline is generally well tolerated
claims.quote: Doxycycline, a broad-spectrum tetracycline antimicrobial, is well absorbed and tolerated

claims.text: Most side effects resolve after stopping
claims.quote: Most adverse effects resolve with discontinuation of the medication.

claims.text: Most common side effects include GI symptoms, esophageal irritation and sun sensitivity (FAQ)
claims.quote: Adverse effects most associated with doxycycline include photosensitivity and gastrointestinal symptoms including esophageal erosion and ulceration

claims.text: Take on a full stomach with full glass of liquid; do not lie down for 1 hour to prevent esophagitis
claims.quote: taking doxycycline on a full stomach with a full glass of liquid and avoiding lying down for 1 hour after taking doxycycline to prevent esophagitis.

claims.text: Separate dose by at least 2 hours from dairy, antacids, and calcium, iron, magnesium or sodium bicarbonate supplements
claims.quote: separating the doxycycline dose by at least 2 hours from dairy products, antacids, and supplements that contain calcium, iron, magnesium, or sodium bicarbonate.

claims.text: Do not take more than 200 mg in 24 hours; as soon as possible, no later than 72 hours (FAQ, dosing paragraph, misconceptions)
claims.quote: Patients should not take more than 200 mg of doxycycline per 24 hours; doses should be taken as soon after sex as possible, but no later than 72 hours.

claims.text: Trials advised taking the dose ideally within 24 hours (FAQ, dosing table)
claims.quote: oral doxycycline hyclate 200 mg self-administered ideally within 24 hours but no later than 72 hours after condomless anal, oral, or vaginal sex

claims.text: Ongoing need reassessed every 3 to 6 months; enough doses until next visit
claims.quote: The prescription should account for enough doses on the basis of the person’s anticipated sexual activity until their next visit. Ongoing need for doxy PEP should be assessed every 3–6 months.

claims.text: PEP means taking a medicine after a possible exposure to prevent infection; doxycycline used preventively for malaria and Lyme disease
claims.quote: Postexposure prophylaxis (PEP) involves taking a medication to prevent an infection after a possible exposure

claims.text: Doxycycline is already used preventively for malaria and Lyme disease
claims.quote: Doxycycline is used as PrEP or PEP to prevent infections such as malaria and Lyme disease

claims.text: June 2024: CDC published its doxy PEP clinical guidelines (record date 2024-06-06)
claims.quote: This report outlines CDC’s recommendation for the use of doxycycline postexposure prophylaxis (doxy PEP), a novel, ongoing, patient-managed biomedical STI prevention strategy for a selected population.

claims.text: Event-driven: taken after sex, not on a daily schedule (key takeaway, FAQ)
claims.quote: CDC recommends that providers offer persons in this group a prescription for doxy PEP to be self-administered within 72 hours after having oral, vaginal, or anal sex.

claims.text: Doxy PEP is prevention, not treatment; symptoms need testing and treatment (misconceptions)
claims.quote: Screen and treat as indicated for sexually transmitted infections (STIs)

claims.text: STI and HIV testing every 3 to 6 months (citable summary, FAQ)
claims.quote: Persons who are prescribed doxy PEP should undergo bacterial STI testing at anatomic sites of exposure at baseline and every 3–6 months thereafter.

claims.quote: The number needed to treat to prevent a quarter with an incident STI was 4.7 in the PrEP cohort and 5.3 in the PLWH cohort.

claims.text: Participants counseled to take 200 mg ideally within 24 hours, no later than 72 hours after condomless sex
claims.quote: Participants were counseled to take 200 mg of doxycycline ideally within 24 hours but no later than 72 hours after any condomless anogenital, vaginal, or oral sex and to take no more than one dose every 24 hours.

claims.text: No serious adverse events attributed to doxycycline
claims.quote: Five grade 3 adverse events and no serious adverse events were attributed to doxycycline.

claims.text: 2% of participants assigned to doxycycline stopped because of unacceptable adverse events or preference
claims.quote: Of participants assigned to the doxycycline groups, 2% discontinued because of unacceptable adverse events or patient preference.

claims.text: Tetracycline-resistant gonorrhea in 5 of 13 isolates with doxycycline vs 2 of 16 with standard care; few cultures available
claims.quote: Of the participants with gonorrhea culture available, tetracycline-resistant gonorrhea occurred in 5 of 13 in the doxycycline groups and 2 of 16 in the standard-care groups.

claims.text: Few gonorrhea cultures available
claims.quote: the number of available gonorrhea cultures was low.

claims.text: Timeline 2023: DoxyPEP found lower rates of gonorrhea, chlamydia, and syphilis
claims.quote: The incidences of the three evaluated STIs were lower with doxycycline than with standard care

claims.text: Trial allowed up to one dose a day
claims.quote: The DoxyPEP study permitted up to daily administration of doxycycline, with a median of 4 doses reported per month

claims.text: People using doxy PEP should be tested for STIs and HIV every 3 to 6 months
claims.quote: Patients on doxy PEP should test for STI and HIV every 3 - 6 months as appropriate.

claims.text: Offer HIV PrEP to those at risk
claims.quote: Discuss and facilitate access to HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for those who are HIV negative, not on HIV PrEP, and at risk for HIV

claims.text: Take with at least 8 ounces of water and food to reduce nausea, upset stomach, and esophageal irritation
claims.quote: Take doxy PEP with at least 8 ounces of water and food. This can help reduce side effects like nausea, upset stomach, and esophageal irritation

claims.text: Wear sunscreen or cover up
claims.quote: Wear sunscreen or cover up to stay protected from the sun while taking doxycycline

claims.text: Separate from dairy, antacids and iron, calcium or magnesium supplements by two hours (FAQ)

claims.text: 2024 to 2026: CDC using existing data systems to monitor uptake, STI rates, prescribing, and resistance
claims.quote: CDC, along with federal partners and other research organizations, is leveraging existing data systems to monitor the uptake of doxy PEP and how this impacts bacterial STI rates, understand national doxycycline prescribing rates, and identify potential development of antimicrobial resistance.

claims.text: CDC will update guidelines as new data become available
claims.quote: As additional data are available from CDC systems and any other research in the field, CDC will update the guidelines.

claims.text: CDC will use multiple data systems to monitor for increases in antimicrobial resistance
claims.quote: CDC will continue to use multiple data systems to help monitor for any increases in antimicrobial resistance associated with doxy PEP implementation.

claims.text: CDC focuses doxy PEP on groups where it has proven effective rather than offering it broadly

claims.text: Providers discuss known and unknown risks; reassessment at follow-up

claims.text: Reassess need at follow-up visits
claims.quote: During these visits, reassess whether there is an ongoing need for doxy PEP.

claims.text: To date, doxy PEP has proven effective only in MSM and transgender women
claims.quote: To date, doxy PEP has only proven effective among gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men and transgender women at increased risk for STIs
